claim: Active fundamental transfer magnitude follows F03 > F06 > F08 at both controlled AC amplitudes.
boundary: This is a descriptive ordering, not a universal impedance law.

claim: Excitation frequency primarily determines branch-selectivity geometry within the frozen 2RC model-replay evidence.
evidence_scope: EXT2 structural and practical identifiability bridge.
boundary: This statement is limited to the current frozen-model replay.

claim: Increasing AC amplitude primarily increases model-replay signal strength while leaving branch-selectivity ratios nearly unchanged.
boundary: Higher amplitude can also alter downstream CV memory.

claim: F03 is the strongest current candidate for slow-branch R2/tau2 information.
boundary: This does not qualify continuous R2/tau2 adaptation.

claim: F06 behaves as a mixed intermediate information region between slow- and fast-branch excitation.
boundary: No direct released online-estimator evidence exists for F06.

claim: F08 shifts dynamic information toward the fast branch relative to F03 and F06.
boundary: Fast-branch practical sensitivity remains weak relative to R0.

claim: At fixed AC amplitude, R0 model-replay voltage sensitivity is approximately frequency-independent across F03, F06, and F08.
evidence_scope: R0 interpretation audit of the controlled decision matrix.
boundary: Approximate equality is limited to the current frozen-model replay.

claim: F08 uniquely maximizes R0 voltage sensitivity.
boundary: Not supported. F08 is special because of the validated gate and direct estimator evidence, not because R0 sensitivity is uniquely higher.

claim: Gated Bayesian R0 adaptation is qualified within the released v1.0 evidence scope.
boundary: This is not unconditional all-timescale R0 adaptation.

claim: A universal 5.38 percent estimator improvement applies across eligible conditions.
boundary: Not supported. Estimator benefit is condition-dependent.

claim: Continuous R1/tau1 online adaptation is qualified.
boundary: Not qualified because practical information is too weak under the available periodic excitation.

claim: Continuous R2/tau2 online adaptation is qualified.
boundary: Not qualified and closed because the measured optimum was not transferable across operating conditions.

claim: Simultaneous continuous R1/tau1/R2/tau2 adaptation is qualified.
evidence_scope: EXT2 structural and practical identifiability analysis.
boundary: Not qualified. Event-based or batch re-identification remains a plausible future route.

claim: The F03 0.3C+0.4C condition has protocol-level post-charge relaxation evidence.
boundary: Same physical-run identity is not established.

claim: The 12-hour relaxation voltage can be treated as equilibrium OCV.
boundary: Not supported. The 12-hour point is only a descriptive long-rest reference.

claim: The observed CV-memory differences are causally attributable to frequency or amplitude.
boundary: Causality is not established because independent replication and full confound control are absent.
Not established. A controlled chamber campaign is required.
Not established. Multiple independent MJ1 cells are required.

claim: The apparent local fundamental transfer is equivalent to small-signal EIS impedance.
boundary: This terminology is not allowed; the result is reported as a local fundamental transfer quantity.
